solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A most unfriendly conclusion regarding part of leg

parts.note: taken as written
superlative of chill, cold in manner
a conclusion is an end
on can mean about or regarding, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: Someone's frostiest parting words concern a bit of somebody's leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regarding' does double duty in the reading: it supplies ON at the end of ACHILLES TENDON rather than linking.
explanation.definitionFit: The Achilles tendon is the cord joining the calf muscle to the heel bone, an anatomical piece of the lower limb.

clue.text: Expert in two sciences collecting a second award, thus is on time

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second
a trophy is a prize or award
Latin sic, meaning thus, used to flag a quoted error
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A scientist with two specialities picks up another prize, and is punctual about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collecting' just joins definition to wordplay; 'thus' is the Latin sic used by editors, and 'on' puts the time abbreviation last.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrophysicist combines astronomy and physics, so is a specialist straddling two scientific disciplines.

clue.text: Hard American musicians to manage carefully

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
US is short for American
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A tough American band needs careful handling by its manager.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb, not the spouse: to husband resources is to use them sparingly.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, husband means to conserve or use thriftily, which is careful management of resources.

clue.text: Flock found wandering in Italy

indicators.note: letters that are wandering stray from their places and end up in a new order

parts.note: the country name, used for its letters

explanation.surface: A flock of sheep is spotted roaming the Italian countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flock' looks like sheep but is the church sense: a priest's congregation, the non-clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor's flock is the ordinary churchgoers, the body of lay people as distinct from clergy.

clue.text: Diplomat joining emirs, say, having made right move

indicators.note: the right-hand letter is told to shift position, so the joined letters come out in a new order

parts.note: Arab rulers, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diplomat joins some emirs and makes the correct move in negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one letter shifts: R, the abbreviation for right, moves from after EMI to after the double S.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is an envoy sent on a mission, a representative much like a diplomat.

clue.text: Before taking power, grow one root crop

parts.note: to grow (pale, say) is to turn
Roman numeral for one
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A farmer, before getting electricity, grows a single crop.
explanation.walkthrough: Grow is used as in 'grow cold', meaning become, so TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnip is a vegetable cultivated for its swollen edible root, a classic field crop.

clue.text: Strange thing to see before autumn, even for poet

indicators.note: something strange is odd or out of the ordinary, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word thing, rearranged
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: A curious sight before autumn, even for a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adverb but is the poetic noun, short for evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Even is an archaic, poetic word for evening, the time of day when dusk arrives.

clue.text: Open University introducing smart purge

parts.note: OU is the abbreviation for the Open University, Britain's distance-learning university
to smart is to sting with pain

explanation.surface: A university brings in a clever clear-out of its staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like an adjective meaning clever; it is the verb meaning to hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A purge is the removal of unwanted people, which is an ousting or expulsion.

clue.text: What's funny about men cavorting with sons? It's practically obvious

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the others

parts.note: comical means funny

indicators.note: people cavorting leap about wildly, so these letters jump into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comic scene of men larking about with their sons, all perfectly obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's funny' looks like a question but is a plain synonym that splits open to hold the jumbled family members.
explanation.definitionFit: Commonsensical describes what plain practical judgement makes evident, sound and sensible rather than theoretical.

clue.text: More irritable about providing witness

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: testy means irritable; testier is the comparative
providing means if, as in providing it rains

explanation.surface: A crankier person ends up giving evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: Testy is an everyday word for short-tempered, and 'providing' works as a conjunction, as in 'providing it rains'.
explanation.definitionFit: A testifier gives evidence under oath, which is what a witness does in court.

clue.text: American soldier's way of working gadget

parts.note: GI is an American soldier; the 's adds S
MO is modus operandi, Latin for a method of operating

explanation.surface: An American soldier's method of operating a gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: Gismo (or gizmo) is informal for a clever device or contraption.

clue.text: Zero change in part of flower

parts.note: the figure zero looks like the letter O
to change is to vary

explanation.surface: No change at all in a section of a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany the ovary is the base of the pistil, the organ of a flower containing the ovules.

clue.text: Most of the mission involved religion

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter
something involved is tangled and complicated, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word the, missing its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Most of a missionary effort was taken up with religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Shintoism is the native religion of Japan, centred on worship of spirits called kami.

clue.text: Part-time medic and explorer land in Westminster

parts.note: Mr Hyde is the alter ego of Stevenson's Dr Jekyll, so the doctor part of the time
Mungo Park, Scottish explorer of the Niger

explanation.surface: A locum doctor and an explorer go to ground somewhere in Westminster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part-time medic' is not a locum: Dr Jekyll spends part of his time as Mr Hyde.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyde Park is the large royal park in central London, lying in the City of Westminster.

clue.text: Choral music playing with no end of harmony, absorbing child

indicators.note: absorbing means taking something inside itself
with no says a letter is to be left out

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: 'end of' keeps only the last letter of 'harmony'

parts.note: the final letter of harmony is the one dropped
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A choir performs without its final harmony, taking in a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: The deletion comes first; the child then slips in just before the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong is unaccompanied medieval church chant, sung in unison by a choir.

clue.text: Difference between scores? It's where notes go

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the winning gap in a match or vote
second meaning: the blank edge of a page, used for jottings

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scores' and 'notes' both suggest music, but one is a game result and the other jottings.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin is both the gap by which a contest is won and the blank border of a page for annotations.

clue.text: Secure border in record time — they'll soon be gone

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
to hem is to secure a border of cloth by folding and stitching
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Tie down a frontier in record time before everything vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record time' reads as a phrase meaning very fast, but it is two separate pieces with the border sitting between them; an EP is an extended-play single.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are short-lived things, transient items of only passing use or interest.

clue.text: Subscribe like Abraham Lincoln, initially? That's notable

parts.note: to subscribe a document is to sign it

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters, here the initials of a name

parts.note: the initials of the president

explanation.surface: Signing one's name with initials as Abraham Lincoln did: that's remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal as an adjective means striking or outstanding, as in a signal achievement.

clue.text: Endlessly annoy one pope? He did!

definitions.text: Endlessly annoy one pope? He did!

indicators.note: endlessly means without the final letter

parts.note: to annoy is to gall; the final L is dropped
Roman numeral for one
Leo is a name taken by many popes

explanation.surface: Who kept on vexing a pope? This man did.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the astronomer's heliocentric views famously irritated Pope Urban VIII and led to his trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo, tried by the Inquisition in 1633, is history's best-known scientist to have provoked papal displeasure.

clue.text: Dessert or kind of bed that prevents you going straight to sleep

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a baked fruit pudding

definitions.text: kind of bed that prevents you going straight to sleep
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a prank bed with the sheet folded so legs cannot stretch out

explanation.walkthrough: An apple-pie bed is a British boarding-school prank: the sheet is doubled back so the victim cannot get in.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a fruit tart served as pudding and the practical-joke bed made with a folded sheet.

clue.text: Path one rebuilt for carriage

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a different form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A track reconstructed to take a horse-drawn vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A phaeton is a light open four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, named after Helios's son.

clue.text: Proceed cautiously, adding a little extra to low digit

parts.note: a tip is a small extra payment
a toe is a digit at the bottom of the body

explanation.surface: Go carefully, adding a little extra to the lowest number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low digit' suggests a small number, but the digit is on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To tiptoe is to walk quietly and warily on the balls of the feet, so to move with care.

clue.text: Caught African animal in European plant

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
the eland is an African antelope
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: An African animal is trapped inside a plant from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but it is simply the letters IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Celandine is a yellow-flowered wild plant, either the lesser celandine or the greater celandine poppy.

clue.text: Part of school collapses following regular expulsions

indicators.note: regular expulsions throw out every other letter, keeping the rest

parts.note: the odd letters of collapses

explanation.surface: A section of the school falls apart after repeated exclusions.
explanation.definitionFit: A class is a group of pupils taught together, one division of a school.

clue.text: Bones coming from fish, I must conclude

parts.note: the carp is a freshwater fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fishbones, I am forced to deduce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conclude' looks like reasoning; it means I comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpi is the plural of carpus, the group of small wrist bones.

clue.text: Burst of fire from Pole, maybe after swapping the middle round

indicators.note: swapping the middle exchanges the two central letters, giving a new order

parts.note: a Pole is one example of a Slav
the letter O is round

explanation.surface: A volley comes from a Polish gunner after changing round in mid-battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole, maybe' is a definition by example: a Pole is one kind of Slav. Only the central L and A trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, a single concentrated volley of fire.

clue.text: Hypothetical article or reference taken back

parts.note: the definite article
taken as written

indicators.note: taken back means read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to cite is to refer to a source

explanation.surface: A speculative newspaper article or citation is withdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Theoretic is a variant of theoretical, meaning based on theory or supposition rather than fact.

clue.text: King, say, shielded by company of people, like those in services

indicators.note: something shielded by another sits protected inside it

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
national means of a people or nation
GR is Georgius Rex, King George
e.g. means for example, as in say

explanation.surface: A monarch is protected by a body of people.
explanation.walkthrough: The king is Georgius Rex, the royal cipher of Britain's six King Georges; with 'say' added, he sits inside the company-plus-people pair just after its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Congregational relates to a congregation, the body of worshippers who attend church services.
